name: Li Wei
appears_on: Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2017-2022)

name: Timur Rahimkulov
forbes_bio: Timur Rahimkulov and his younger brother, Ruslan, became billionaires after inheriting the fortune from their father, Megdet, who led the Hungarian office of Russian gas giant Gazprom in the early 1990s.
Megdet Rahimkulov became CEO and co-owner of a joint venture between Gazprom and Hungary's oil and gas concern MOL in the mid 1990s.
The elder Rahimkulov also headed AEB, a Hungarian bank that Gazprom bought to process payments from its local customers that he later bought from Gazprom.
At the same time, he started began buying shares of MOL and OTP, Hungary's largest bank.
The brothers, both of whom live in Hungary, inherited the wealth in 2020 and began diversifying into other assets, including real estate.
forbes_facts: Their father Megdet Rahimkulov was the richest person in Hungary before his return to Russia in 2008.

name: Youssef Mansour
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Youssef Mansour is chairman of family-owned conglomerate Mansour Group, which was founded by his father Loutfy (d. 1976) in 1952.
Mansour Group is the exclusive distributor of GM vehicles and Caterpillar equipment in Egypt and several other countries.
He oversees the consumer goods division, which includes supermarket chain Metro, and sole distribution rights for L'Oreal in Egypt.
Younger brothers Mohamed and Yasseen are also billionaires and part owners of Mansour Group.
forbes_facts: Former Egypt President Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalized his father's original cotton trading business.
Mansour is a founding member of the American Egyptian Chamber of Commerce.

name: Zhou Yongli
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2018-2020); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhou Yongli chairs Yongli Group, a business with interests in trading, real estate and finance.
Yongli, headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Shaoxing in Zhejiang Province, was established in December 1986.

name: Igor Tulchinsky
forbes_bio: Igor Tulchinsky is founder and CEO of WorldQuant, a quantitative investment firm with $17 billion in assets under management.
WorldQuant specializes in stastical arbitrage and other quantitative-driven trading techniques.
Born in Belarus, Tulchinsky immigrated to the U.S. as a child and began his career at AT&T Bell Laboratories.
He spent two years at Interactive Brokers before moving to Millennium, the hedge fund run by billionaire investor Izzy Englander.
He founded WorldQuant in 2007 as a subadvisor of Millennium, and it still manages $7 billion on behalf of the larger hedge fund.
forbes_facts: His nonprofit WorldQuant University provides free online masters-level courses in financial engineering.
He has written three books about investing and financial markets.

name: Renato dos Santos
forbes_bio: Renato Monteiro dos Santos is one of the partners of BTG Pactual Holding, the holding company of BTG bank, with about 2/3 of its assets.
Banco BTG Pactual is a Brazilian investment bank and asset and wealth manager that was founded in 1983 and now has with more than 1 billion reais ($200 million) under management.
He began his career at BTG Pactual in 1997 as a trader and now serves as senior vice president of the bank, responsible for its Latin America Treasury Department.
dos Santos is a member of BTG's managers group -- the 'Top Seven Partners' -- together with fellow billionaire Roberto Balls.

name: Laszlo Szijj
forbes_bio: László Szíjj is the cofounder and owner of Duna Aszfalt, a leading construction company for roads and bridges in Hungary.
Szijj bought out his former Duna partner and childhood friend, Károly Varga, to become sole owner of the business in 2019.

The business, which grew rapidly beginning in the mid 2000s on government contracts, has more recently looked outside of Hungary for growth, acquiring peer companies in Romania, the Czech Republic and Poland.
Szijj is also a business partner of Lőrinc Mészáros, Hungary's richest person, and owns two yachts where he has hosted several members of the Hungarian political and economic elite.

name: Ben Ashkenazy
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Ben Ashkenazy bought his first building at age 17, after he went to a Bronx  shopping center to check out a site to open a fast food restaurant.
Then a recent high school grad, Ashkenazy realized the lease offered was below market value and decided to find a lender and buy the property instead.
Since then he's built a portfolio of stakes in more than 100 buildings via real estate firm Ashkenazy Acquisitions, which he founded and runs as CEO.
The company owns historical landmarks like Washington D.C.'s Union Station and Boston's Faneuil Hall.
Ashkenazy, who primarily invests in retail properties, is also a minority owner in New York's famed Plaza Hotel.
forbes_facts: In between his real estate ventures, Ashkenazy took night classes at Adelphi University but ended up six credits shy of graduating.

name: Sasson Dayan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Lebanon-born Sasson Dayan founded Brazil's Banco Daycoval in 1968 with his brother Ibrahim Dayan.
Daycoval has become one of Brazil's biggest lenders to small and mid-sized businesses, and also provides personal banking services.
Dayan transferred almost all his shares in Daycoval to his three sons in 2015, whose stakes are included in the family fortune.
Dayan remains president of the bank's board, while daily operations are headed by his sons and nephew.
forbes_facts: Dayan got his start working at a banking firm in Lebanon founded by his father.

name: Christina Flügel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Christina Flügel is a fifth-generation member of the Mast-Jägermeister family fortune, best known for its green-bottled herbal liquor.
Her brother, Florian Rehm, a fellow German billionaire, chairs the company and serves as its spokesperson.
Mast-Jägermeister was founded in 1878 as a maker of vinegar; it shifted to producing wine and spirits in 1922 before creating the now-famous recipe for Jägermeister.

name: Sergei Kolesnikov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Sergei Kolesnikov owns 50% of Technonicol, a global producer of roofing, waterproofing and thermal insulation materials.
He is a managing partner of Technonicol, which owns 72 companies and factories in seven countries in Europe and Asia.
Kolesnikov founded the company with his classmate Igor Rybakov in 1992.
Kolesnikov financed an ecopark near Ryazan with an area of more than 500,000 square meters with a hotel complex and biathlon track.
forbes_facts: Kolesnikov finances biathlon schools and built two biathlon stadiums.
Together with colleagues from Technonicol, Kolesnikov participates in sailing competitions.

name: Neide Helena de Moraes
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Neide Helena de Moraes is an heir to a stake in Grupo Votorantim, a Brazilian industrial conglomerate.
She is a granddaughter of Jose Ermirio de Moraes, who founded Grupo Votorantim in 1918; she previously appeared on Forbes? billionaires list in 2014.
The company does business in more than 20 countries in the aluminum, pulp and paper, energy, banking and cement industries.
Neide Helena inherited an 8% stake in the family-owned company after the death of her father, Jose Ermirio de Moraes Filho, in 2001.
Her two siblings, Jose Ermirio de Moraes Neto and Jose Roberto Ermirio de Moraes, also inherited Votorantim stakes from their father.

name: Daniela Grogg
forbes_bio: Daniela Grogg is the daughter of Peter Grogg, founder of Swiss biochemical company Bachem Holding AG.
Peter Grogg, who died in 2025, started the business in 1971 and served as CEO until 2002, and chairman until 2012.
Grogg, along with her billionaire sister and mother, all serve on the board of the family's asset management firm Ingro Finanz AG.
Bachem AG develops and manufactures active pharmaceutical ingredients, including peptides, amino acid derivatives and other organic molecules.
The family controls about 58% of Bachem as well as shares in Swiss electrical engineering company Burkhalter Holding and chemical maker Dottikon.
forbes_facts: In 1971, Grogg started Bachem with 50,000 Swiss Francs.

name: Norma Lerner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Norma Lerner is the widow of Al Lerner (d. 2002), who made a fortune as founder of credit card giant MBNA.
Al started his career as a furniture salesman, invested in Cleveland-area real estate and bought control of Equitable Bancorp in 1981.
Equitable Bancorp and Maryland National formed the credit card giant MBNA, which was acquired by Bank of America for $35 billion in 2005.
forbes_facts: The family sold the English football club Aston Villa for $88 million to Chinese businessman Tony Xia in 2016 after a decade of ownership.
They bought the Cleveland Browns in 1999 and brought pro football back to the city, but sold the team to billionaire Jimmy Haslam for about $1 billion in 2012.
